svg.text: Service Barge – Bow Cut-Out and Portal Hoist
Service barge with bow cut-out and portal hoist
4 no. HYDRAULIC CLAMPS TO THE UNIT HANGER LUGS
UNIT LIFTED CLEAR OF THE WATER
Isolate the unit and lock off at the shore switchgear.
Barge noses bow-first over the unit; spud legs drop fore and aft to hold station.
Portal hoist runs out over the cut-out; 4 no. hydraulic clamps close on the hanger lugs.
Sub-frame pins are released and the unit is hoisted clear of the water, still clamped.
Work is done on the barge deck in air, or the spare unit carried aft is swapped in.
Unit is lowered, pinned back to the sub-frame, clamps released, spuds raised, barge off.
Dock-mounted units, where a forklift cannot reach.
Mid-river and estuary arrays on moored sub-frames.
Recovery, inspection and blade change away from site.
INDICATIVE ARTIST'S ILLUSTRATION – NOT TO SCALE
Dimensions to be confirmed by survey and detailed design
Service vessel for the whole fleet. It works dock units, mid-river arrays, island moorings, pylon rigs and offshore wind foundations.
Barge 18 000 x 8 000 mm with a 4 000 x 6 000 mm cut-out in the bow, giving working access to the unit from three sides at once.
The barge noses over the unit, four hydraulic clamps engage the same hanger lugs the sub-frame uses, and a portal hoist lifts the unit clear of the water.
Spud legs are dropped fore and aft to hold station against the current while the unit is lifted; no anchoring over the array is required.
Work is done on the barge deck, in air, with the unit still clamped. A spare unit is carried aft so the array is only ever one unit down.
One barge covers a fleet of docks and rigs. Sizing, freeboard, stability and spud reach to be confirmed at detailed design.
